We know nothing about this from the stored knowledge. Neither the client store nor the firm store contains anything on Joad's supplier history, supplier audits, or any supplier-qualification program. I'd be guessing if I described them.

**What the stored knowledge does cover (and why it matters here):**
- **Records are sensitive.** The firm treats a client's internal design, testing and complaint records as sensitive, and supplier audit and qualification files probably fall in the same category. Joad will not stipulate to authenticity or produce anything beyond what the court requires until a protective order is signed. That order needs an outside-counsel-and-experts-only tier.
- **Access runs through Thorsby.** All case communications go through General Counsel Evander Thorsby. We should not contact Joad engineers, production staff or purchasing and quality personnel directly. Thorsby arranges access, and we should discuss any Joad witness with him before putting that person forward.
- **Tight circle.** Joad wants a tight circle around who sees test files. We should apply the same discipline to any supplier materials we receive.
- **Experts.** If we need a standards or supplier-quality expert, Joad must approve the name and credentials before engagement. It has offered to help identify candidates with standards-body experience.

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Ask Thorsby what supplier records exist. That would cover the supplier list and history for the JX-series spindle components, audit reports, corrective-action records, and the qualification procedures and approvals.
2. Ask who at Joad knows the program, and have Thorsby arrange access.
3. Get the protective order in place before any of it is produced or authenticated.
4. Check whether the pleadings or discovery requests in C-2 put supplier issues in play. I don't have those documents.

If you have other files on C-2, such as the complaint, discovery requests or earlier correspondence, send them and I can look for supplier information there.
